title: Microsoft Teams: allowed list of external meeting notetaker bots
summary: Hold: the briefing describes detected bots as always waiting for admission, but current guidance also documents automatic blocking without lobby admission. Microsoft now explains recovery for some people incorrectly blocked as bots, so the briefing's uncertainty about existing blocked participants is outdated. The roadmap details, admin path and approval command are supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Existing bot detection uses signals collected during the meeting join process.
claims.quote: Teams uses built-in detection mechanisms to identify external AI bots based on signals collected during the meeting join process.

claims.where: What's changing: existing external-bots setting
claims.claim: The existing setting places detected bots in the lobby irrespective of the meeting's lobby configuration.
claims.quote: Block all detected bots: Detected bots are automatically blocked from joining the meeting. They aren't placed in the meeting lobby for organizer approval, and meeting organizers can't admit them.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence beginning 'Learn says Teams detects' with: 'Learn says Teams detects external bots from signals collected during the join process. Under When detected, require approval before joining, detected bots are placed in the lobby irrespective of the meeting's lobby configuration.'

claims.where: What's changing: Detected bots require explicit admission
claims.claim: Detected bots require explicit admission under the existing setting without qualification by policy mode.
claims.quote: Detected external bots are automatically blocked from joining meetings. They can't be admitted by meeting organizers or other participants.
claims.fix: Replace 'Detected bots require explicit admission' with 'Under that approval option, detected bots require explicit admission'. This refers to When detected, require approval before joining, not Block all detected bots.

claims.where: What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The external-bots guide says presenters may admit bots under the approval option, depending on the meeting setting.
claims.quote: Organizers (also presenters, depending on the meeting setting), need to explicitly admit these bots into the meeting.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The Bot Identification Program page describes detected bots as requiring organizer approval even when participants can bypass the lobby.
claims.quote: Even when a meeting allows participants to bypass the lobby, detected bots still require organizer approval before joining.

claims.where: What's changing: existing default option; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The existing external-bots setting defaults to When detected, require approval before joining, or RequireApprovalWhenDetected.
claims.quote: RequireApprovalWhenDetected: When detected, bots will be enforced to the meeting lobby, regardless of the lobby setting of the meeting. They will require approval before getting access to the meetings. This is the default value.

claims.where: What's changing: default option; Governance controls: second row explanation
claims.claim: RequireApprovalWhenDetected holds detected bots in the lobby until explicitly admitted.
claims.quote: Detected external bots are placed in the meeting lobby and require explicit approval before joining.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
